quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Apostrophes (Names Ending in S) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: James book was left on the bus
quests.punctuatedSentence: James's book was left on the bus.
quests.ruleExplanation: For a singular name ending in s, add both an apostrophe and an s to show possession, as in 'James's.'
quests.nativeTip: Even though this name already ends in s, singular possession still adds an apostrophe and another s.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: James book was left on the bus ➔ Final: James's book was left on the bus.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Apostrophes (Names Ending in S) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Chris car needs new tires
quests.punctuatedSentence: Chris's car needs new tires.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Chris's' takes an apostrophe and an s, following the standard rule for singular possessives.
quests.nativeTip: Treat this name the same way you would any other singular noun, even though it already ends in s.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Chris car needs new tires ➔ Final: Chris's car needs new tires.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Apostrophes (Names Ending in S) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Lucas backpack was stuffed with textbooks
quests.punctuatedSentence: Lucas's backpack was stuffed with textbooks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since only one person named Lucas owns the backpack, the possessive form adds an apostrophe and an s.
quests.nativeTip: This name ends in s, but it's still only one person owning the backpack.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Lucas backpack was stuffed with textbooks ➔ Final: Lucas's backpack was stuffed with textbooks.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Smiths house has a red door
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Smiths' house has a red door.
quests.ruleExplanation: When a plural family name already ends in s, the possessive adds only an apostrophe after it, as in 'the Smiths'.'
quests.nativeTip: This refers to the whole Smith family together, not just one person.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Smiths house has a red door ➔ Final: The Smiths' house has a red door.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Garcias new restaurant opens next week
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Garcias' new restaurant opens next week.
quests.ruleExplanation: A plural family name ending in s becomes possessive with just an apostrophe added at the end.
quests.nativeTip: More than one Garcia owns this restaurant - the whole family.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Garcias new restaurant opens next week ➔ Final: The Garcias' new restaurant opens next week.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Andersons cabin is up in the mountains
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Andersons' cabin is up in the mountains.
quests.ruleExplanation: The plural possessive of a family name already ending in s only needs an apostrophe after the s.
quests.nativeTip: Picture the entire Anderson family owning this cabin together.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Andersons cabin is up in the mountains ➔ Final: The Andersons' cabin is up in the mountains.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Names Ending in S (Discrimination) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Travis guitar was out of tune
quests.punctuatedSentence: Travis's guitar was out of tune.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since Travis is a single person, the possessive adds an apostrophe and an s.
quests.nativeTip: Only one person named Travis owns this guitar.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Travis guitar was out of tune ➔ Final: Travis's guitar was out of tune.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Names Ending in S (Discrimination) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Davises garden won an award this year
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Davises' garden won an award this year.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because the plural family name already ends in s, the possessive form only adds an apostrophe after it.
quests.nativeTip: This refers to the whole Davis family, not just one person.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Davises garden won an award this year ➔ Final: The Davises' garden won an award this year.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Names Ending in S (Discrimination) (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Marcus essay won first place in the contest
quests.punctuatedSentence: Marcus's essay won first place in the contest.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since only one person named Marcus is being discussed, the singular possessive takes an apostrophe and an s.
quests.nativeTip: Compare this to a family name - is this one person or a whole family?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Marcus essay won first place in the contest ➔ Final: Marcus's essay won first place in the contest.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Jack and Emmas apartment has a great view
quests.punctuatedSentence: Jack and Emma's apartment has a great view.
quests.ruleExplanation: When two people jointly own a single thing, only the last name in the pair takes the possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: They share one apartment together, so only the second name needs the apostrophe.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Jack and Emmas apartment has a great view ➔ Final: Jack and Emma's apartment has a great view.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Tom and Sofias wedding was held outdoors
quests.punctuatedSentence: Tom and Sofia's wedding was held outdoors.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the wedding belongs to both of them jointly, only Sofia's name takes the apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This is one shared event that belongs to both of them together, not two separate things.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Tom and Sofias wedding was held outdoors ➔ Final: Tom and Sofia's wedding was held outdoors.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Maria and Davids business is doing well
quests.punctuatedSentence: Maria and David's business is doing well.
quests.ruleExplanation: A single item owned jointly by two people only needs an apostrophe on the second name.
quests.nativeTip: One shared business belongs to both partners together.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Maria and Davids business is doing well ➔ Final: Maria and David's business is doing well.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Jacks and Emmas phones both need to be charged
quests.punctuatedSentence: Jack's and Emma's phones both need to be charged.
quests.ruleExplanation: When each person owns a separate item, both names take their own possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: Each person has their own separate phone, not one phone shared between them.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Jacks and Emmas phones both need to be charged ➔ Final: Jack's and Emma's phones both need to be charged.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Toms and Sofias opinions on the movie were very different
quests.punctuatedSentence: Tom's and Sofia's opinions on the movie were very different.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the opinions belong to each person individually, both names need their own apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: These are two separate, individual opinions rather than one shared idea.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Toms and Sofias opinions on the movie were very different ➔ Final: Tom's and Sofia's opinions on the movie were very different.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Marias and Davids offices are on different floors
quests.punctuatedSentence: Maria's and David's offices are on different floors.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because each office belongs to a different person, both names take their own possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: Each person has their own individual office, located separately.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Marias and Davids offices are on different floors ➔ Final: Maria's and David's offices are on different floors.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Shared vs. Separate Possession (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Ben and Ritas car broke down on the highway
quests.punctuatedSentence: Ben and Rita's car broke down on the highway.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since they share one car together, only 'Rita' gets the possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: Decide whether this is one shared vehicle or two separate ones.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Ben and Ritas car broke down on the highway ➔ Final: Ben and Rita's car broke down on the highway.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Shared vs. Separate Possession (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Bens and Ritas schedules rarely line up
quests.punctuatedSentence: Ben's and Rita's schedules rarely line up.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because each person has a separate schedule, both names take their own possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: Each of them has their own individual schedule, not one shared calendar.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Bens and Ritas schedules rarely line up ➔ Final: Ben's and Rita's schedules rarely line up.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Shared vs. Separate Possession (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Aisha and Toms presentation impressed the whole board
quests.punctuatedSentence: Aisha and Tom's presentation impressed the whole board.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the presentation was created together, only the second name, 'Tom,' takes the possessive apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This is one shared project they worked on together, not two separate presentations.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Aisha and Toms presentation impressed the whole board ➔ Final: Aisha and Tom's presentation impressed the whole board.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: We bought three banana's at the market
quests.punctuatedSentence: We bought three bananas at the market.
quests.ruleExplanation: A plain plural noun like 'bananas' never needs an apostrophe unless it's showing possession.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether this word is showing ownership or simply naming more than one banana.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: We bought three banana's at the market ➔ Final: We bought three bananas at the market.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The stores closing hour's are posted on the door
quests.punctuatedSentence: The store's closing hours are posted on the door.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Store's' needs an apostrophe to show the hours belong to the store, but 'hours' is simply plural and needs no apostrophe at all.
quests.nativeTip: Two words here need attention - one is missing an apostrophe, and one has one that doesn't belong.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The stores closing hour's are posted on the door ➔ Final: The store's closing hours are posted on the door.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: My parent's are visiting next week
quests.punctuatedSentence: My parents are visiting next week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the sentence simply refers to more than one parent, no apostrophe is needed at all.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence isn't describing something that belongs to the parents - it's just talking about more than one parent.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: My parent's are visiting next week ➔ Final: My parents are visiting next week.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The company updated its employee handbook
quests.punctuatedSentence: The company updated its employee handbook.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the handbook belongs to the company, 'its' is possessive and should not have an apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether this word means 'it is' or shows something belonging to it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The company updated its employee handbook ➔ Final: The company updated its employee handbook.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The dogs in the shelter need new home's
quests.punctuatedSentence: The dogs in the shelter need new homes.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Homes' here is just a plural noun and doesn't need an apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This word is simply plural, describing more than one home, not showing ownership.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The dogs in the shelter need new home's ➔ Final: The dogs in the shelter need new homes.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Wilson's are hosting a barbecue this weekend
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Wilsons are hosting a barbecue this weekend.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since nothing is being shown as belonging to the Wilson family here, the name stays a plain plural with no apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence is just naming the whole family, not showing that something belongs to them.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Wilson's are hosting a barbecue this weekend ➔ Final: The Wilsons are hosting a barbecue this weekend.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Its a shame the teams captain wont be playing
quests.punctuatedSentence: It's a shame the team's captain won't be playing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It's' means 'it is,' 'team's' shows singular possession of the captain, and 'won't' needs its apostrophe for 'will not.'
quests.nativeTip: This sentence has three separate apostrophe decisions - a contraction, a possessive, and another contraction.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Its a shame the teams captain wont be playing ➔ Final: It's a shame the team's captain won't be playing.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Petersons dog wont stop barking at its own shadow
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Petersons' dog won't stop barking at its own shadow.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Petersons'' shows the family owns the dog, 'won't' needs an apostrophe, and 'its' stays without one since it already shows possession.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs a family possessive, a contraction, and a correctly unmarked possessive word.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Petersons dog wont stop barking at its own shadow ➔ Final: The Petersons' dog won't stop barking at its own shadow.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Whos going to tell Marcus that his cars keys are missing
quests.punctuatedSentence: Who's going to tell Marcus that his car's keys are missing?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who's' means 'who is,' 'car's' shows singular possession of the keys, and the sentence ends with a question mark since it's asking something.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs a contraction, a possessive noun, and the right end punctuation.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Whos going to tell Marcus that his cars keys are missing ➔ Final: Who's going to tell Marcus that his car's keys are missing?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Chris and Jamies project wont be finished by Friday
quests.punctuatedSentence: Chris and Jamie's project won't be finished by Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since they share one project, only 'Jamie' takes the possessive apostrophe, and 'won't' needs its own apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This is one shared project they're working on together, and a contraction needs fixing too.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Chris and Jamies project wont be finished by Friday ➔ Final: Chris and Jamie's project won't be finished by Friday.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The Millers are selling they're old furniture
quests.punctuatedSentence: The Millers are selling their old furniture.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The Millers' stays a plain plural with no apostrophe since nothing here belongs to them, and 'their' shows the furniture belongs to them without needing an apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence just names the family as a group, and a nearby word needs the correct possessive form instead of a contraction.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The Millers are selling they're old furniture ➔ Final: The Millers are selling their old furniture.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Its clear that Lucass essay impressed the judges
quests.punctuatedSentence: It's clear that Lucas's essay impressed the judges.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It's' means 'it is,' and 'Lucas's' takes an apostrophe and an s to show singular possession, even though the name already ends in s.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs a contraction at the start and a possessive apostrophe for a name ending in s.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Its clear that Lucass essay impressed the judges ➔ Final: It's clear that Lucas's essay impressed the judges.
